units.title: Risk Taking
units.intro: This unit asks **why people take risks** in life. You will read short stories (case studies) and think about **risky behaviours**, **sexual risk taking**, and **what makes a risk justifiable**.

pins.text: Case 1: a popular artist, 19, died after a long illness (it was rumoured she had AIDS). She left a baby of six months.
Case 2: a long distance bus hit a bicycle. Two students riding home from school died at the spot.

lessons.title: What makes adolescents vulnerable or invulnerable?

cards.title: What this unit is about
body: By the end of this unit you will be able to find out **why people take risks** in life.
You will also name the **consequences** (results) of risk.

cards.title: Two new words
body: The book asks: what do **vulnerable** and **invulnerable** mean?
**Vulnerable**: you can be hurt easily.
**Invulnerable**: you cannot be hurt.
(These are word meanings to help your English.)

cards.title: Two case studies
body: Tap the dots. Read each story.

cards.title: Case 1: the artist
body: A **popular artist** died after a long illness.
People said for some time that she had **AIDS**.
She was just **19**. She left a **baby of six months** behind.

cards.title: Case 2: the two students
body: A **long distance bus** hit a **bicycle**.
Two students were riding it **home after school**.
Both students **died at the spot**.

cards.title: Think and talk
body: The book asks you to compare the two deaths.
- Which risk has the **least chance** to affect your life? Why?
- Why do adolescents face such problems?
- What do we learn from the case studies?

cards.q: In Case 1, how old was the artist when she died?
cards.why: "She was just 19 when she died" (p. 1). The baby was six months old.

cards.title: What is risk taking?
body: The book asks: **What is risk taking?**
Then you sort **15 behaviours** into three colours.

cards.title: Red, yellow, green
body: Tap each light.

cards.title: Memory trick: the traffic light
body: Like a road light: **red** = stop, **yellow** = be careful, **green** = go.

cards.title: Behaviours in the table (1–8)
head: No.
Behaviour
rows: Driving when drunk
Crossing a road
Having unprotected sex
Walking alone at night
Dropping out of school

Accepting a lift from a person you know

cards.title: Behaviours in the table (9–15)
head: No.
Behaviour
rows: Sleeping without a mosquito net in a mosquito area
Getting married and having children before the age of 20
Riding a bicycle at night without lights
Doing what your friends do
Unprotected sex with your long time boyfriend or girlfriend
Riding a bicycle without holding the handle bars
Going to a disco or party

cards.title: Your turn
body: Put each behaviour under **red**, **yellow** or **green**.
Then think: are these risky behaviours **common in your area**? Why?
The book gives no answer key. Talk with your class and teacher.

cards.q: In the table, what does "yellow" mean?
cards.why: Red = definitely risky, yellow = probably risky, green = not risky (p. 2).

cards.title: Aster and Solomon

states.label: Friends
states.text: Aster (15) and Solomon (17) are classmates since elementary school. In grade 8 they sit on the same bench and do homework together.

states.label: "I love you"
states.text: One day, studying at Aster's house, Solomon says "I love you." Aster says "I love you too."

states.label: What next?
states.text: The book asks: What would **you** do if you were Aster? Will they **abstain** from making love? If not, what problems will they face?

body: Move the slider.

cards.title: Key word: abstain
body: To **abstain** means to choose **not to do** something.
The book asks if Aster and Solomon will abstain from making love, and why.

cards.q: Where were Aster and Solomon when Solomon said "I love you"?
cards.why: "One day while they were studying in Aster's house..." (p. 3).

cards.title: Justifiable or not?
body: A risk can be **justifiable** (there is a good reason for it) or **unjustifiable** (there is no good reason).
The book gives two case studies. You decide.

steps.text: Yonas is **14**. He lives in a **village**.
His mother tells him to collect wood. If he does not, **food will not be cooked**.
The wood is **beyond a river**.
So he **has to cross the river** to bring the wood.

cards.title: Case study 2: Amina
body: Tap the dots to see Amina's problem.

cards.title: Amina's choice
body: Amina does **not want** to have sex.
But she does **not want to lose** her boyfriend too.

cards.title: Questions to discuss
body: - If you were Amina or Yonas, what would you do? Why?
- What advice would you give them?
- If you were Amina's boyfriend, what would you do?
- Which risk is **justifiable**, and which is **unjustifiable**? Why?

cards.q: Why does Yonas have to cross the river?

options.B: because the wood is beyond the river

cards.why: "He saw that woods were beyond a river. So he had to cross the river" (p. 4).

tips.text: Read each case study twice. Find **who**, **how old**, **what happened**.
Traffic light: **red** definitely risky, **yellow** probably risky, **green** not risky.
For "justifiable" questions, ask: **is there a good reason** to take this risk?
Many questions have no single answer. Give a reason for your answer.

questions.q: What is the difference between a justifiable and an unjustifiable risk?
questions.answer: A justifiable risk has a good reason. An unjustifiable risk has no good reason.
why: p. 4–5 asks you to sort the risks into these two groups.
Justifiable = can be justified (defended with a good reason).
questions.tip: Ask: is there a good reason?

units.title: Consequences of Risk Taking
units.intro: This unit is about the **results (consequences)** of taking risks: **accidents**, **tobacco and alcohol**, **STIs**, **HIV** and **pregnancy**. It ends with a picture **project**.

cards.title: What you will learn
body: In this unit you will look at the **feeling of invulnerability** ("nothing bad can happen to me") and its **consequences**.
You will also look at the **effect of tobacco and alcohol**.

steps.text: Tsegay, a grade 8 student, wants to **go home during classes**. He **jumps over the fence**.
He **falls down** and is **seriously injured**.
He gets **first aid**. The director calls an **ambulance**.
The doctor says he has to **sleep in the hospital**.
But his mother **cannot afford** to pay the hospital expenses.

cards.title: One risk, many results
body: One risky jump led to: a **serious injury**, the **hospital**, and **money problems** for his mother.

cards.title: Questions to think about
body: - Why do you think Tsegay took such a risk?
- What advice would you give students like him?
- What common accidents happen in your area?

cards.q: Why did Tsegay jump over the fence?
cards.why: "One day he wanted to go home during classes. While jumping over the fence, he fell" (p. 6).

cards.title: Agree, disagree, not sure
body: The book gives **12 statements** about smoking and alcohol.
Put **√** if you agree, **X** if you disagree, **?** if you are not sure.

cards.title: Statements 1–6
head: No.
Statement
rows: Smoking is not a serious risk like drinking alcohol
Drinking alcohol makes you more confident
People who smoke and drink alcohol should be punished
Smoking is mostly started during teenage years
Alcohol affects some people more than others
Alcohol helps people handle their problems

cards.title: Statements 7–12
head: No.
Statement
rows: Smoking will hurt a pregnant woman but not her baby
Young people are often pressurized to take alcohol by their friends
Most alcoholics end up as homeless people
Inhalants such as glue and benzene are dangerous to health
Both smoking and alcohol constantly damage the lungs
Drinking alcohol/smoking can lead to divorce

cards.title: Four statements to discuss
body: Tap the dots. Do you agree?

cards.title: If you were the director
body: The book asks: if you were the **director** of your school, what **rules** would you make about smoking and alcohol?
And what could help **smokers stop smoking** and **alcoholics stop drinking**?

cards.q: Which two things does statement 10 call "inhalants"?
cards.why: Statement 10: "Inhalants such as glue and benzene are dangerous to health" (p. 8).

cards.title: What are STIs?
body: **STI** stands for **Sexually Transmitted Infection**.
The book asks you: **What are STIs?**

cards.title: Helen's case
body: Helen is a grade 8 student. She lives with her **aunt**.
One day, when her aunt was away, Helen was **raped** (forced to have sex) by her **neighbour**.
She **kept it secret**.

cards.title: Questions the book asks
body: - If you were Helen, what would you do? Why?
- What could happen if she **keeps the rape secret**?
- What **health problems** could Helen face?
- What should the **community** do in such cases?

cards.title: A study tip
body: These are hard questions. Talk about them with your **teacher** or a **trusted adult**.

cards.q: Who did Helen live with?
cards.why: "Helen is a student in grade 8 and lives with her aunt" (p. 9).

cards.title: What does HIV stand for?
body: **HIV** = **Human Immunodeficiency Virus**.

cards.title: The card game
body: Your class plays a card game. Some students get the "A" card.

cards.title: For the "A" card group
body: - Were you expecting the "A" card?
- How did you feel? How do you respond to your feeling?
- In which round did you get "A"?

cards.title: For the rest of the students
body: - Why did some students get the "A" card?
- How do you feel about them?
- Will you **never** get the "A" card if you keep playing?
- What would you do if you got HIV infection?

cards.q: What does the "I" in HIV stand for?
cards.why: HIV = Human Immunodeficiency Virus (p. 9, lesson title).

cards.title: Two close friends
body: **Amina** and **Lemlem** are grade 8 students and very close friends.
They spend most of their time talking about their **boyfriends**.

cards.title: Two decisions

states.label: Amina
states.text: Amina and her boyfriend **agreed not to have sex before marriage**.

states.label: Lemlem
states.text: Lemlem's boyfriend **always asks** her for sex. During a **summer festival**, she spends one night with him.

body: Move the slider.

cards.title: Questions
body: - What would you do if you were Lemlem?
- Do you agree with Lemlem's or Amina's decision? Why?
- How could Lemlem have **avoided** this?

cards.q: When was Lemlem found pregnant?
cards.why: "After one month, she was found pregnant" (p. 10).

lessons.title: Project: risk taking behaviours and their consequences

cards.title: The project
body: Draw each of the **5 statements** as a picture.
Write the **risk taking behaviour** and its **consequence** on each picture.
Then sort them into **justifiable** and **unjustifiable** risks.

cards.title: The five statements
body: Tap each picture.

cards.title: A clue for sorting
body: In statements 1, 2 and 3 the person **says the danger out loud**, but still does the risky thing.
In statements 4 and 5 the person did something needed (travel, an operation) and the bad thing **happened to them**.

cards.q: In statement 2, what does the chain smoker doctor say?
cards.why: Statement 2: "A chain smoker doctor says, Smoking causes lung cancer" (p. 11).

tips.text: For each story, write: **risk** → **consequence**. Example: jumped the fence → injured.
Learn the full names: **STI** = Sexually Transmitted Infection; **HIV** = Human Immunodeficiency Virus.
Agree/disagree tables have no single answer key. Give a **reason** for each answer.
Justifiable or not? Ask: was there a **good reason**, and did the person **know** the danger?

units.intro: This unit helps you **protect yourself**: respecting the **laws and norms** of society, **sensing danger**, being **assertive**, **making and sticking to decisions**, **underage marriage**, **malaria and TB**, and **personal hygiene**.

lessons.title: Laws and norms of the society

cards.title: What you will learn
body: In this unit you will build **decision making**, **assertiveness** and **negotiation** skills.
You will also learn the **causes and prevention** of **malaria** and **tuberculosis**.

cards.title: Case I: at the wedding

states.label: The elders arrive
states.text: The guests immediately **give their seats** to the village elders.

states.label: One boy stays
states.text: A young boy stays in **one of the best seats** beside the elders.

states.label: A whisper
states.text: An elder calls the boy and **whispers** some words. The boy **immediately leaves** his seat.

body: Move the slider.

steps.text: Tesfay **stole** Ato Ahmed's goat.
He **sold** it in the market.
His close friends **Omer and Mebrahtu** informed the police.
He was taken to **jail**.

cards.title: Norms and laws
body: Case I shows a **norm** (a custom of the society): giving your seat to **elders**.
Case II shows the **law**: stealing leads to **jail**.

cards.title: Questions to discuss
body: - Why did the boys leave their seats for the elders?
- What punishment do you suggest for Tesfay?
- What would you do if you were Omer and Mebrahtu?
- What words did the elder whisper?

cards.q: Who informed the police about Tesfay?
cards.why: "Omer and Mebrahtu, Tesfay's close friends, informed the police" (p. 12).

cards.title: The situation
body: Anwar's family went to visit relatives. He is **alone at home**.
He invites **Sara**, his classmate, to come to his home.

cards.title: Sense the danger
body: The book asks:
- What could happen to Sara if she **accepts**?
- Why did Anwar invite her?
- What would **you** do if you were Sara? Why?

cards.title: In your area
body: What **dangers** are common in your area? How could they be **avoided**?

cards.q: Why is Anwar alone at home?

options.B: his family went to visit relatives

cards.why: "Anwar's family went to visit their relatives leaving him alone at home" (p. 13).

cards.title: Two skills
body: **Assertive**: you say clearly and calmly what you want and what you do not want.
**Negotiation**: talking to reach an agreement.
(Word meanings to help your English.)

cards.title: The mini drama: Ahmed and Hayat

steps.text: Ahmed says Hayat looks nice and **invites her to a party**.
Hayat: "**Sorry Ahmed, today I am busy.**"
Ahmed: it is at night and **I have got a car**. Hayat agrees, but says she must **go home early**.
At the party Ahmed says: "I love you so much and I will do everything you need."
Ahmed says he **booked a hotel room**: "let us go there". He says it is a chance they must not miss.
Hayat: "**No Ahmed**, we are together and can do this another time."

cards.title: Questions
body: - Did Hayat act **assertively**? Why?
- What do you think of her **negotiating** skills?
- What can you say about **Ahmed**?
- How would **you** respond if you were Hayat?

cards.q: What did Ahmed say he had booked?
cards.why: "Hayat, now I booked a room in a hotel down town and let us go there" (p. 13).

lessons.title: Decision making and sticking to decisions

cards.title: Hana's decision
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: What Hana did
body: Samson wants Hana to **leave school** and **marry** him. Even her friend Muna agreed with Samson.
But **Hana refused**.

cards.title: Think about it
body: - Was it **easy** for Hana to decide? Why?
- What would happen if she accepted?
- Will she **stick to** her decision?
- What makes a decision **good or bad**?

cards.q: What did Samson want Hana to do?
cards.why: "He... wants Hana to leave school and marry him" (p. 14).

cards.title: The project
body: The book asks: **What is underage marriage?** Is it common in your community?
(**Underage** means younger than the age the law allows.)

cards.title: Consequences to find
head: Area
Question
rows: health
What are the health consequences of underage marriage?
social
What are the social consequences?
economic
What are the economic (money) consequences?

cards.title: Sayings and norms
body: Find **sayings** in your mother tongue that **encourage** or **discourage** underage marriage.
Interview people. Which marriage **norms and laws** would you like to **continue**, and which would you like to **modify** (change)?

cards.q: The project asks about consequences in three areas. Which list is right?
cards.why: p. 15: consequences related to a. health, b. social, c. economic.

cards.title: 3.6.1 Malaria
body: The book asks: **What is malaria?** What are the ways of **preventing** it?

cards.title: Marco's family
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: The case study
body: Marco and his family live in **Tokombia**, near **River Gash**.
Today everyone works to **drain the swamp** and clear bushes around the house.
Only **Silvana** does not: she has a **headache and fever**.

cards.title: Malaria questions
body: - What health problem threatens Marco's family?
- What is the cause of Silvana's illness? How can the family help her?
- What advice would you give **neighbours** and people who **travel** to malaria areas?

cards.title: 3.6.2 Tuberculosis (TB)
body: Mark each statement: **agree**, **disagree** or **not sure**.

cards.title: TB statements 1–5
head: No.
Statement
rows: TB affects only old people
We can avoid TB by taking traditional medicine
People who always cough have TB
Only poor people contract TB
TB can be spread by sharing utensils

cards.title: TB statements 6–10
head: No.
Statement
rows: Coughing among overcrowded people has less chance to spread TB
TB is a curable disease
A person with TB must take medicine under the supervision of a health worker
Rates of TB infection are highest where people are poor and overcrowded
A person with TB must be kept in a separate room

cards.title: TB questions
body: - What are the **symptoms** of TB?
- Why does TB mostly occur where people are **poor and overcrowded**?
- Should a TB patient be kept separately? Why?
- What are the ways of **preventing** TB?

cards.q: Where do Marco and his family live?
cards.why: "Marco and his family live in Tokombia near River Gash" (p. 15).

cards.title: Henok's day
body: Henok is a **14** year old, hard working student.
Every day he **feeds the chickens**, goes to **school**, **looks after the cattle**, and **plays** with friends.

units.title: Building Good Relationships
units.intro: This unit is about **friends**: the **circles of friendship**, **making friends** (pen pals), and **resisting peer pressure**.

acquaintances
A: Abdela, 12, grade 7, 130 cm tall. Likes farm work in summer, reading, children's TV, music. P.O. Box 1718, Asmara.

body: In this unit you learn to take the **right actions**.

cards.title: How is malaria transmitted?

cards.title: The child in Aligidr

cards.title: A common problem
body: Ato Hassen is a **farmer** in **Aligidr**. His **five year old** child died of malaria in **mid September**.
This problem is **common** in most families in Aligidr.
People now use some **protective measures**.

cards.title: Late night coffee
body: But look at what many families do at night.

cards.title: Questions
body: - Are the people taking the **right actions**?
- What should the **community** do to stop the spread of malaria?
- How does **environmental sanitation** help prevent malaria?
- Malaria kills people. Why do people still sleep **without nets** in mosquito areas?

cards.q: Where do many families in Aligidr stay until late at night?
cards.why: "...many of the families stay outside until late night enjoying their coffee ceremony" (p. 22).

cards.title: How is water contaminated?
body: **Water borne** diseases are diseases carried by **water**.
The book asks: **How is water contaminated** (made dirty)?

steps.text: A village in the **southern zone** had little drinking water. People walked **two hours** to fetch water.
In **1993** the **Ministry of Agriculture** built a dam **half a kilometre** from the village.
People got **plenty of water** for their homes and animals.
But the health centre's **laboratory results** showed many people were **infected** with different diseases.

cards.title: Think
body: - What diseases might the people have?
- How can the community keep the water **clean**?
- What can be done **at home** to make dam water safe to drink?
- Is water that **looks clean** always safe to drink? Why?

cards.q: Who built the dam, and when?
cards.why: "In 1993 a dam was built by the Ministry of Agriculture" (p. 23).

cards.title: Air borne diseases
body: **Air borne** diseases are carried through the **air**.
Mark each statement: **√** agree, **X** do not agree, **?** do not know.

cards.title: Statements 1–4
head: No.
Statement
rows: Only poor people are infected by air borne diseases.
If you are coughing, you have got TB.
Air borne diseases can be transmitted by food and water.
HIV positive and HIV negative people have equal chance of being infected with TB.

cards.title: Statements 5–8
head: No.
Statement
rows: Smoking cigarette enhances air borne disease infection.
Air borne diseases are spread by sexual intercourse.
The spread of TB is fast in overcrowded area.
Many air borne diseases have no cure.

cards.title: Questions
body: - Can traditional medicines treat air borne diseases? How?
- **Who** needs more care concerning air borne diseases? Why?
- How can air borne diseases be **prevented**?
- What should the **community** do?

cards.title: Tecle and Idris
body: Idris went to the **school meeting**. Tecle asks what it was about.

steps.text: Idris went to the school meeting.
Next **Sunday** there is a **cleaning campaign**. Tecle does not want to work on Sunday. Idris agrees they need rest. But he says: "Our area is **full of rubbish**." Attendance will be taken.
Students must **bring materials**.
**Machines** will level the ground. They will **load the rubbish on cars**.
Tecle: "Why don't you burn the rubbish?" Idris: "They ordered us **not to burn anything**."

cards.title: Questions
body: - Why were the students told **not to burn** the rubbish?
- What advice would you give Tecle?
- What could we use **instead of plastic bags** to carry goods?
- What should the community do to keep the environment **clean and healthy**?

cards.q: What were the students ordered not to do?
cards.why: Idris: "They ordered us not to burn anything" (p. 26).
